## Goal
`tests/test_netpolicy.py` and `tests/test_qa_v03_review.py:31-60` check listed hosts, user-info, backslashes, control characters and loopback opt-in with a handful of hand-picked inputs. Nothing checks the allow-list's invariants over a table of hostile spellings, or the set algebra of `for_broker` and `with_loopback`.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. `host_of` (`src/freemyid/netpolicy.py:38-54`): over a table of at least 30 hostile or odd inputs (mixed case, trailing dot, `[::1]`, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, explicit ports, `%2e` in the host, punycode `xn--` lookalikes, empty user-info `https://@host`, tab/NBSP/zero-width characters, `javascript:` and `data:` URLs, scheme-relative `//host`) the result is either None or a lower-case host with no trailing dot, whitespace or backslash, and `host_of(host_of(x)) == host_of(x)` whenever it is not None.
2. `NetPolicy.is_allowed` (84-86) is never true for a host that is not an allowed entry or a subdomain of one: suffix lookalikes (`evilfakepeople.example`, `fakepeople.example.evil.example`) are refused; case and one trailing dot never change the answer (`_norm` 24-25, `_host_ok` 28-30).
3. `for_broker` (88-102): the result is always a subset of the policy's allowed hosts, and never contains a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.2`, `x.localhost`, `::1`; `_is_loopback` 33-35) unless the policy opted in.
4. `with_loopback` (77-82) returns a copy: the original policy's `allowed` set and `allow_loopback` flag are unchanged afterwards.
5. `captcha_subresource_allowed` (121-139), cases not already in `tests/test_d9_security_fixes.py:113-125`: explicit `:443` allowed, `:8443` refused, `/recaptcha` (no slash) and `/recaptchaX/` refused, `sub.www.google.com` refused, `api.hcaptcha.com` allowed, a main-frame navigation always refused.

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
